# `iscope_stop_view`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Stop the current view (full stop) or one named stage of it.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (full command-socket call; shared diagnostic writes; 64-bit and 32-bit builds) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xde080 (64-bit build) |

Without a usable stage string the whole view is stopped: view mode returns to none, device shoot status is cleared, binary sending stops and the view workers stop. With a stage string only that named function is stopped; an unknown or not-running name is not an error. A stopped function ends with a cancel event (no code or error on the wire; internal code 253, not sent); on a full stop the View event then repeats with mode none (application to View INFERRED). In one special full-stop case (main stacking active with the wide camera selected) the handler puts the wide camera to sleep, switches back to the main process and returns without writing result or code, so that reply carries only the envelope members. Stops join worker threads and can block; no total timeout is established. The grade reflects the whole request/reply path, which reaches the shared diagnostic logger; it does not by itself mean the method changes device settings.

Side effects: Stops view stage workers or the whole view; full stop saves filter position, stops the named star worker or leaves the live-stream page, resets stack, mosaic and continuous-capture state on applicable branches and can close the focuser; stage Stack may clear photometry data; 64-bit local AutoExp stop records an aborted capture error. May relay to the second camera process (10000 ms per wait). Every call also performs shared request/reply diagnostic logging.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"iscope_stop_view"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | no | - | Optional. Only the stage member is read. Absent, null, scalar, array or empty-object params, and a missing or non-string stage, all take the full-stop path (no error). A positional array wrapping the object is not unwrapped, so it also performs a full stop. [READ] |
| `params.stage` | string | no | - | Optional string. Any string, including empty or unknown, selects stage-stop; AutoExp, AutoGoto and Stack have explicit case-sensitive branches, everything else is passed to the stop-by-name helper without error. Names the app sends: 3PPA, AutoExp, DarkLibrary, AutoGoto, Initialise, ObjectTrack, ScanSun, Stack (these are app-sent names, not a firmware enum). 32-bit build lacks the AutoExp special case. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (success) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | integer | yes | - | (success) For these methods the result is the integer 0. Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (success) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 536 | A ViewPlan worker is running (every input shape) | `view plan is already running` |
| 210 | 64-bit build: stage AutoExp on the main process while the current mode is star without wide support, or the mode id is 6 or above | `not supported` |
| 300 | Relay to the other process has no user-data context | `internal error` |
| 207 | A relay failure left the error code zero | `fail to operate` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Relay slave errors are copied through; the full relay error universe is not established.

## Example

Request, full-stop - Stop the whole view:

```json
{"id":31,"method":"iscope_stop_view"}
```

Request, stop-stage - Stop one stage (name is one the app sends):

```json
{"id":32,"method":"iscope_stop_view","params":{"stage":"AutoGoto"}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"iscope_stop_view","result":0,"code":0,"id":32}
```

Reply, plan-running:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"iscope_stop_view","error":"view plan is already running","code":536,"id":33}
```
